A command contract points to a concrete reference SDK/source and reproducible raw oracle result; no latest-only identity is accepted.
Noun-first and retained legacy package/reference forms have separately tested parsing and equivalent reference edits where upstream supports both.
Unsupported options fail without project/cache/install mutations; help and version commands work without a feed.
A generic-arity, illegal-identifier or runtime gap remains blocked instead of passing after a silent public rename.
Changing the reference patch invalidates affected contract evidence and produces a reviewed compatibility diff.
A clean environment with only the locked JDK and source can build the seed and first SDK without a circular dependency.
Paths containing spaces and Unicode reach javac and child applications unchanged on each advertised OS.
Missing or incompatible JDK fails before producing a success marker or incomplete installation.
Cancellation terminates owned children and leaves reusable previous outputs intact.
The seed-built and SDK-rebuilt outputs satisfy the declared reproducibility comparison with all nondeterministic inputs explained.
Equivalent conditional project inputs select the same conceptual references and target order as the locked reference fixture.
Directory.Build props/targets and command-line property overrides follow the qualified precedence with no hidden second evaluator.
Editing a solution preserves unrelated projects/comments and reports unsupported project types explicitly.
A compiler, package, generated-source or target change invalidates the affected cache, while a no-change build reuses verified outputs.
Clean and cancellation cannot delete source files or another configuration/project output tree.
Console and classlib templates create compilable projects with exact framework API names and no Maven/Gradle requirement.
Dry-run leaves the filesystem unchanged while identifying intended outputs and conflicts.
A template archive or transform attempting to escape its output root is rejected before writes.
A requested C# language option cannot silently generate Java and claim equivalent language support.
Repeated installation/uninstallation preserves user files and removes only template-owned state.
A local Java-profile package restores and builds; a same-ID CLR-only package is rejected before compilation.
Locked restore reproduces the graph and content hashes; changed dependency metadata or payload bytes fail without silently rewriting the lock.
Package source mapping prevents unintended source selection, including an inherited public CLR feed.
Interrupted or concurrent downloads never expose partial cache entries; corrupt/path-traversal packages are rejected.
A complete local package closure restores offline, while a missing transitive package produces a named deterministic failure.
New, restore, build and run complete a working two-project application with source-verified framework APIs.
No-restore/no-build behavior matches the selected command contract and cannot silently fetch or compile missing inputs.
A real failing test causes the expected nonzero result and report; a crashed runner cannot be counted as passing.
Application arguments and exit status survive launcher forwarding, including spaces and Unicode.
A reference/JVM differential check rejects an altered default, missing warning or wrong exit code instead of normalizing it away.
Side-by-side SDKs select the expected version for each qualified global.json case without altering DOTNET_ROOT or unrelated JAVA_HOME.
A missing exact SDK with roll-forward disabled fails locally and does not silently download a replacement.
Interrupted/corrupt installation leaves the previous version runnable and no staged version advertised as installed.
Uninstalling one SDK preserves another SDK and packs still referenced by it.
An offline full bundle installs, creates, restores locally, builds and runs its declared sample without network access.
Framework-dependent output runs with an eligible runtime and clearly fails when that runtime is absent or incompatible.
Self-contained output runs on the qualified clean OS/architecture without a preinstalled JDK or dotj SDK.
Local publish creates complete local outputs and performs no unrequested remote deployment or upload.
A missing native asset or incompatible runtime identifier fails before publication is declared successful.
A JAR, jlink image or restart loop cannot satisfy a NativeAOT, single-file or hot-reload parity test without its actual required behavior.
Local tool restore/run follows the checked-in manifest and cannot overwrite an unrelated CLR/global tool installation.
A tool command collision fails or follows the locked reference behavior without silently hijacking another executable.
Failed workload update preserves the previous usable workload, and shared packs survive removal while still referenced.
An incompatible platform or missing required external tool is reported before a workload is marked installed.
IDE and terminal builds select the same SDK, project configuration and dependencies for the same fixture.
The client discovers resource URLs from the service index and restores the Java-profile package using the qualified protocol.
Same-ID/version publication with different bytes is rejected and cannot make a partially uploaded artifact visible.
Expired credentials, throttling and service failure produce bounded retry/error behavior with no secrets in logs.
Restoring a backup yields metadata whose content hashes and downloadable artifacts all agree.
Package downloads already published remain recoverable when search or nonessential portal components are unavailable.
Equivalent source/toolchain inputs run through provider-independent build steps and satisfy the declared artifact reproducibility check.
Artifacts lacking a required notice, signature, manifest or platform acceptance result cannot be promoted.
A Git import alone is never reported as migrating pipeline secrets, work items or branch protections.
Changing source host does not silently break existing immutable package/download references.
Failed promotion leaves the previous channel usable and does not overwrite a previously released package version.
All 66 products have a distribution disposition and owner, including products not yet implemented.
Every advertised public API preserves its source-verified name/case and every claimed command behavior has named passing evidence.
A new developer completes the qualified create/add/build/test/publish path without Maven, Gradle or a new framework vocabulary.
Unimplemented mobile/browser/AOT or language gaps remain visible and cannot be hidden behind a blanket exact-parity claim.
The final report distinguishes written requirements, executed tests, implemented capabilities and release authorization status.
